response:
Diagnosis. Two results from generation 4 reorganize the search. First, the champion (asset-lightness × cycle-averaged earnings yield: fmb 5.46, alpha 3.4%, t 3.55, Sharpe 0.48) was not improved by any grid recombination — durability, total-capital denominators, per-current-capital normalization and peak anchors all landed at alpha 1.5-2.6%, so the moderator/denominator grid is exhausted. Second, and more informative, the earnings-shortfall construct failed *decisively in the opposite direction* (alpha -2.9%, t -3.34): firms whose current profit sits below their own five-year norm underperform reliably. That is a strong new fact, not a dead end — its mirror image, a price-scaled *surplus* of current over normal earning power, is an untested channel with a t-statistic of comparable magnitude already implied. Since normalized yield and the surplus are additive components of the spot yield, this batch tests the surplus mirror, the spot-yield decomposition, the surplus as a moderator rather than a price-scaled level, one full consolidation of the two proven moderators, and two economically distinct refinements to the normalization itself (per-share dilution adjustment and a shrinking-business guard).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: MoatDurability_x_EarningsSurplusOverNorm
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(oiadp, at), 0.1), 5), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, MA(oiadp, 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Investors under-react to the amount by which a franchise firm's current operating profit exceeds its own five-year norm when that excess is large relative to market value; the market treats the improvement as transitory even for firms with proven durable returns, so the surplus is not yet in the price.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The generation-4 shortfall construct produced an alpha of -2.9% with t -3.34, which is direct evidence that this price-scaled deviation carries reliable information with the sign reversed, and the reversed version is economically the more sensible one because it aligns with rather than against the profitability premium. Keeping the durability gate matters: a surplus over norm is only credible evidence of earning power for firms that have repeatedly cleared a high return hurdle, otherwise it is a one-year windfall.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_SpotOperatingEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: If both the cycle-average level of earning power and the current excess over that average are priced too cheaply, then the simple spot operating-earnings yield — which is exactly their sum — should carry the combined effect, and it should do so most strongly for asset-light firms whose reported operating profit is not consumed by reinvestment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the decisive decomposition test for the whole normalized-yield family: the archive shows the averaged component predicts positively (t 3.55) and the deviation component predicts positively once its sign is corrected (implied t 3.34), so their sum should dominate unless the two components' portfolio exposures offset. It costs no coverage — no five-year lag is required — which also tells us whether the champion's five-lag requirement was buying anything.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: OwnNormProfitSurprise_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(oiadp, at), MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness against mid-cycle earning power is most trustworthy when the firm is currently earning above its own historical return on capital, because that combination means the low price reflects stale expectations rather than a business operating below its own norm.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This asks whether the own-norm deviation works better as a bounded conditioner on the proven valuation leg than as a price-scaled level (Signal 1), which is a genuine structural question rather than a rescaling: as a moderator it is scale-free and cannot be dominated by market-cap variation, whereas as a valuation term it inherits the price denominator. It also replaces the profitability-level and trend moderators already tested with a firm-relative deviation, a conditioner dimension the archive has not used.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: DurableAndAssetLight_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(oiadp, at), 0.1), 5), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at)))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durability and capital lightness protect normalized cheapness for different reasons — one says the profit stream persists, the other says it is not consumed by reinvestment — so a firm that is cheap on mid-cycle earning power and satisfies both conditions is the cleanest instance of profitable value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Each moderator alone produced roughly 2.6% and 3.4% alpha against the same valuation leg, so the consolidation question of whether their information is complementary or overlapping is now the highest-value question in the archive and cannot be answered by either parent. Both weights are bounded and non-negative, so the signed valuation leg still governs the spread and coverage is unaffected since both moderators use data already required by the yield.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_PerShareNormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, csho), 5), prcc_f), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Normal earning power should be measured per share against price, because averaging historical dollar profits over a period in which the firm issued equity credits today's shareholders with profits they did not own; per-share normalization automatically penalizes serial diluters and rewards firms that shrank their share count.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a substantive economic correction to the champion rather than a scaling variant: aggregate normalization is dilution-blind, so a firm that doubled its share count looks as cheap as one that bought back stock, and share-count history is exactly the information the market is documented to underweight. Holding the asset-lightness moderator fixed isolates whether dilution-adjusted normalization improves the strongest signal in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RevenueGrowthGuard_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(sale, 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A cycle-averaged earnings yield is mechanically highest for businesses in structural decline, whose average includes better years that will never return; requiring that the revenue base is still expanding separates genuinely mispriced normalized value from melting ice cubes.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This targets the specific known weakness of Graham-style normalization — backward-looking averages flatter shrinking firms — with a conditioner that is not a profitability level, trend, volatility or durability measure but the trajectory of the business base itself, so it is a new moderator dimension for this archive. If it lifts alpha above the champion, the residual risk in normalized value is decline rather than distress, which would redirect the remaining generations toward growth-guarded normalization rather than further quality gates.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE MoatDurability_x_EarningsSurplusOverNorm---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Because the durability gate is non-negative, SUB(oiadp, MA(oiadp,5)) is the exact negation of the already-evaluated MoatDurability_x_EarningsShortfallFromNormal, so the results are mechanically known (fmb ≈ +1.96, alpha ≈ +2.9%, t ≈ +3.34) up to winsorization asymmetry and the test adds no new information — the honest move is to re-label the sign convention of the existing signal, not spend a generation rerunning it.

---CRITIQUE AssetLightness_x_SpotOperatingEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A clean and coverage-cheap ablation that correctly decomposes the normalized yield into level plus deviation and asks whether the five-year smoothing earns its keep, though the valuation leg reduces to plain EBIT/P (a long-known anomaly) so the only novelty resides in the capital-intensity moderator already established in the archive.

---CRITIQUE OwnNormProfitSurprise_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Recasting the own-norm deviation as a scale-free bounded rank moderator on the proven normalized-yield leg is a legitimate structural question rather than a rescaling, but it overlaps materially with the already-tested TREND and ACCEL moderators of ROA, so the incremental information is modest.

---CRITIQUE DurableAndAssetLight_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Stacking the two best-performing moderators against the same valuation leg is a defensible complementarity-vs-redundancy test with no coverage cost, but multiplying two bounded weights compresses the effective cross-section and makes it the kind of incremental consolidation that will be hard to interpret if alpha lands between the two parents.

---CRITIQUE AssetLightness_x_PerShareNormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated mechanism is backwards — averaging historical per-share profits computed on smaller past share counts *flatters* serial diluters, whereas dividing averaged dollar profits by today's market cap already embeds the enlarged share base, so the expression penalizes exactly the opposite firms from those the hypothesis claims.

---CRITIQUE RevenueGrowthGuard_x_NormalizedEarningsYield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent attack on the specific known failure mode of backward-looking normalization using a moderator dimension (top-line trajectory) the archive has not tried, though it works against the documented negative pricing of growth/investment, so a null or attenuated result would be as informative as a positive one and should be interpreted accordingly.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AssetLightness_x_DemonstratedEarningPowerYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MAX(oiadp, MA(oiadp, 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The right anchor for value is a firm's demonstrated earning capacity, defined as the greater of what it earns today and its own mid-cycle norm: the norm rescues firms in a temporary trough, while current profit rescues firms whose five-year average is stale because the business has genuinely improved, and cheapness against that anchor is the mispricing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is not the negation of the archived shortfall signal, whose result is mechanically known — the MAX anchor is a non-linear envelope of the two proven components rather than their difference or their sum, so it is not recoverable from any previously evaluated expression. It also encodes a specific economic asymmetry the archive has not tested: the averaged anchor and the spot anchor each fail for an identifiable group of firms, and the envelope fails for neither, which should raise the slope without the coverage cost of extra conditioning.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: PerShareEarningPowerGrowth_x_NormalizedEarningsYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 3), csho), 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(oiadp, 5), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Only earning power per share accrues to existing owners, so cheapness against mid-cycle profit is real value when smoothed operating profit per share has been rising, and largely illusory when aggregate profit grew only because the share base was expanded to fund it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The mechanism is now stated in the direction the arithmetic actually runs: dividing smoothed profit by the *current* share count each year and taking its three-year growth mechanically penalizes firms that issued equity and rewards those that retired stock, which is the opposite of averaging stale per-share history. The moderator is a profitability trajectory measured at the owner level rather than per asset — a conditioner dimension not yet tested — and it is paired with the archive's best valuation leg so the comparison against the champion isolates the dilution-adjusted growth channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
